% Source: manuscript/parts/part2/ch19_cld_examples.tex and its included
% residual-Picard dossier.
\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:p213-residual-picard-smooth-curve}
Let $K$ be algebraically closed, complete, and nontrivially valued, let
$C$ be a smooth proper algebraic $K$-curve, and let
$W\subset C^{\mathrm{an}}$ be open.  Suppose that
$h\in C^0(W,\mathbf R)$ satisfies
\[
                         \dprimeddprime[h]=0.
\]
For a type~$2$ point $x\in W$, let $C_x$ be its smooth projective
residue curve and let
\[
 \operatorname{ob}_x(h)\in
 \operatorname{Pic}^0(C_x)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf R
\]
be the residual class of the harmonic germ of $h$ at $x$.  Then the
following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $h$ is ordinary CLD-smooth near $x$ and
      $\dprimeddprime h=0$ there as a smooth form;
\item $\operatorname{ob}_x(h)=0$.
\end{enumerate}
At points of types $1$, $3$, and $4$, the germ of $h$ is automatically
ordinary CLD-smooth with zero smooth Hessian.

Consequently, if
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p213-residual-picard-vanishing}
       \operatorname{Pic}^0(C_x)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf R=0
       \qquad\text{for every type~$2$ point }x\in W,
\end{equation}
then $h$ is ordinary CLD-smooth on $W$ and
$\dprimeddprime h=0$ as a smooth form.  The hypothesis
\eqref{eq:p213-residual-picard-vanishing} holds, in particular, when the
residue field $\widetilde K$ is algebraic over a finite field, or when
$C$ is a Mumford curve.
\end{proposition}

% Source: manuscript/editorial/solver_dossiers_20260919/
% p062_interleaved_polyannulus_mixed_towers_20260919/STATEMENT.tex.
\begin{theorem}
\label{thm:p062-interleaved-polyannulus-mixed-bundle-towers}
Let $K$, $C$, and $W\subset C^{\mathrm{an}}$ be as in
\Cref{thm:wanner-curve-comparison}, let $\ell\geq1$, and put $B_0=W$.
Suppose that
\[
 B_\ell\xrightarrow{\pi_\ell}B_{\ell-1}
 \longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow B_1
 \xrightarrow{\pi_1}B_0
\]
is a finite tower in which every $B_j$ is a positive-dimensional good,
topologically separated, boundaryless, pure strict $K$-analytic space.  At
every stage assume that exactly one of the following descriptions is
specified.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The morphism $\pi_j$ is a locally trivial standard strict
open-polydisc bundle as in
\Cref{prop:p062-open-polydisc-bundle-descent}; in particular, its positive
fibre dimension and chart radii satisfy the conditions there.
\item The base $B_{j-1}$ is locally holomorphically separated and
paracompact, and $\pi_j$ is a locally trivial analytic projective-space
bundle as in \Cref{prop:p062-projective-bundle-descent}, with fibre
$(\mathbf P_K^{q_j})^{\mathrm{an}}$ for some $q_j\geq1$.
\item The base $B_{j-1}$ is locally holomorphically separated and
paracompact, and $\pi_j$ is a locally trivial smooth proper split-toric
bundle as in
\Cref{prop:p062-smooth-proper-split-toric-bundle-descent}, with fibre
$X_{\Sigma_j}^{\mathrm{an}}$ for a smooth proper split toric $K$-variety
$X_{\Sigma_j}$ of dimension $q_j\geq1$.
\item The base $B_{j-1}$ is locally holomorphically separated and
paracompact, and $\pi_j$ is a locally trivial proper smooth curve bundle as
in \Cref{prop:p062-proper-smooth-curve-bundle-descent}, with fibre
$D_j^{\mathrm{an}}$ for a nonempty geometrically connected smooth proper
algebraic $K$-curve $D_j$.
\item There are an integer $s_j\geq1$ and standard strict open annuli
\[
 A_{j,k}=\{z\in(\mathbf G_{\mathrm m,K})^{\mathrm{an}}:
                 r_{j,k}<|T_{j,k}(z)|<R_{j,k}\},
 \qquad 0<r_{j,k}<R_{j,k},\quad r_{j,k},R_{j,k}\in|K^\times|,
\]
for $1\leq k\leq s_j$, together with an isomorphism over $B_{j-1}$
\[
 B_j\simeq B_{j-1}\times_K\prod_{k=1}^{s_j}A_{j,k}
\]
under which $\pi_j$ is the first projection.  Write
$q_{j,k}:B_j\to A_{j,k}$ for the corresponding projection.
\end{enumerate}
Let $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,\ell\}$ be the set of stages of the fifth
type, put
\[
 \Pi=\pi_1\circ\cdots\circ\pi_\ell:B_\ell\longrightarrow W,
\]
and, for $j\in J$, put
\[
 \rho_j=\pi_{j+1}\circ\cdots\circ\pi_\ell:B_\ell\longrightarrow B_j,
 \qquad
 L_{j,k}=\rho_j^*q_{j,k}^*\log|T_{j,k}|,
\]
where $\rho_\ell$ is the identity when $\ell\in J$.  If
$h\in C^0(B_\ell,\mathbf R)$ satisfies
$\mathrm d'\mathrm d''[h]=0$, then there are unique continuous functions
\[
 b:W\to\mathbf R,
 \qquad a_{j,k}:W\to\mathbf R\quad(j\in J,\ 1\leq k\leq s_j)
\]
such that
\[
 h=\Pi^*b+
   \sum_{j\in J}\sum_{k=1}^{s_j}(a_{j,k}\circ\Pi)L_{j,k},
 \qquad \mathrm d'\mathrm d''[b]=0,
\]
and every $a_{j,k}$ is locally constant.  In particular, $h$ is
classically pluriharmonic, locally $\mathbf R$-PL, and
Gubler--Jell--Rabinoff harmonic.
\end{theorem}

% Source: manuscript/parts/part2/ch15_poincare_lelong.tex.
\begin{lemma}
\label{lem:ch15-log-smooth}
Let $f$ be an invertible analytic function on an open set $U\subset X$.
Then $\log|f|$ is a smooth function on $U$ in the sense of ordinary CLD
forms, and
\[
 \dprime\log|f|=-\dprime t,\qquad
 \ddprime\log|f|=-\ddprime t,\qquad
 \dprimeddprime\log|f|=0,
\]
where $t$ is the affine coordinate on $\mathbf R$ pulled back by the moment
map $f$, that is, $t=-\log|f|$.
\end{lemma}

% Source: manuscript/parts/part2/ch13_forms.tex.
\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:cld-form-pullback}
Let $g:Y\to X$ be a morphism of topologically separated analytic spaces.
There is a functorial morphism
\[
                 g^*:A_X^{p,q}\longrightarrow g_*A_Y^{p,q}
\]
commuting with wedge, $J$, $\dprime$, and $\ddprime$.
\end{proposition}

% Source: manuscript/parts/part2/ch16_bedford_taylor.tex.
\begin{corollary}
\label{cor:ch16-smooth-h}
Let $U$ be open in a good, topologically separated, pure, boundaryless
strict analytic space, let $T$ be a positive closed ordinary CLD current on
$U$, and let $u,v$ be continuous functions on $U$ satisfying
$\dprimeddprime[u]=\dprimeddprime[v]$.  If $h=u-v$ is ordinary CLD-smooth
and $\dprimeddprime h=0$, then
$\dprimeddprime(hT)=0$, equivalently
$\dprimeddprime(uT)=\dprimeddprime(vT)$.
\end{corollary}

% Source: manuscript/parts/part6/ch72_major_open_problems.tex.
\begin{problem}
\label{prob:frontier-cross-fan-upstairs}
Let $K$ be a complete non-Archimedean field, let $n\geq2$, and let $X$
be a good separated strict boundaryless pure $n$-dimensional
$K$-analytic space.  Determine whether every positive
$\mathrm d'$- and $\mathrm d''$-closed CLD current $T$ of bidegree
$(p,p)$, $0\leq p\leq n-1$, has the following property: for every open
$W\subseteq X$ and all continuous psh functions $U,V$ on $W$,
\[
                  \mathrm d'\mathrm d''[U]
                  =\mathrm d'\mathrm d''[V]
\]
implies
\[
 \mathrm d'\mathrm d''\bigl(U\,T|_W\bigr)
 =\mathrm d'\mathrm d''\bigl(V\,T|_W\bigr).
\]
If this fails, construct a counterexample.
\end{problem}

% Source: manuscript/parts/part2/ch19_cld_examples.tex.
\begin{theorem}
\label{thm:wanner-curve-comparison}
Let \(K\) be algebraically closed, complete, and nontrivially valued, let
\(C\) be a smooth proper algebraic curve, and let \(W\subset C^{\mathrm{an}}\)
be open.  For a continuous function \(u:W\to\mathbf R\),
\[
                  \dprimeddprime[u]\geq0
        \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
                  u\text{ is Thuillier-subharmonic}.
\]
Consequently every continuous CLD-psh function on \(W\) is
Thuillier-subharmonic.
\end{theorem}

% Source: manuscript/parts/part2/ch19_cld_examples.tex.
\begin{corollary}
\label{cor:ch19-continuous-zero-current-harmonic}
Under the hypotheses of \Cref{thm:wanner-curve-comparison}, let
$h:W\to\mathbf R$ be continuous.  If
\[
                         \dprimeddprime[h]=0,
\]
then $h$ is Thuillier harmonic, hence harmonic in the sense of
Gubler--Jell--Rabinoff and classically pluriharmonic in the sense of
Gubler--Rabinoff.
\end{corollary}

% Source: manuscript/parts/part2/ch18_delta_forms.tex.
\begin{lemma}[First-current rigidity on a published curve]
\label{lem:p062-curve-first-current-rigidity}
Let \(K\), \(C\), and \(W\subset C^{\mathrm{an}}\) be as in
\Cref{thm:wanner-curve-comparison}.  If \(b\in C^0(W,\mathbf R)\) satisfies
\[
          \mathrm d'\mathrm d''[b]=0,\qquad \mathrm d'[b]=0,
\]
then \(b\) is locally constant.
\end{lemma}

% Source: manuscript/parts/part2/ch18_delta_forms.tex.
\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:p062-open-polyannulus-rigid-base}
Let \(K\) be a complete non-Archimedean field with nontrivial absolute
value, let \(m\geq1\), and let \(B\) be a good, topologically separated,
boundaryless, pure \(m\)-dimensional strict \(K\)-analytic space.  Assume
that
\begin{enumerate}
\item every \(b\in C^0(B,\mathbf R)\) satisfying
  \(\mathrm d'\mathrm d''[b]=0\) is classically pluriharmonic; and
\item every \(b\in C^0(B,\mathbf R)\) satisfying
  \(\mathrm d'\mathrm d''[b]=0\) and \(\mathrm d'[b]=0\) is locally
  constant.
\end{enumerate}
For \(s\geq0\), let
\[
 A_i=\{z\in(\mathbf G_{\mathrm m,K})^{\mathrm{an}}:
                     r_i<|T_i(z)|<R_i\},
 \qquad 0<r_i<R_i,\quad r_i,R_i\in|K^\times|,
\]
and put
\[
 X_s=B\times_K\prod_{i=1}^sA_i,
 \qquad p:X_s\longrightarrow B,
 \qquad q_i:X_s\longrightarrow A_i.
\]
If \(h\in C^0(X_s,\mathbf R)\) satisfies
\(\mathrm d'\mathrm d''[h]=0\), then there are unique continuous
functions \(b,a_1,\ldots,a_s:B\to\mathbf R\) such that
\[
 h=p^*b+\sum_{i=1}^s(a_i\circ p)q_i^*\log|T_i|,
 \qquad \mathrm d'\mathrm d''[b]=0,
\]
and every \(a_i\) is locally constant.  In particular, \(h\) is
classically pluriharmonic.  Moreover, every
\(u\in C^0(X_s,\mathbf R)\) satisfying
\[
             \mathrm d'\mathrm d''[u]=0,
             \qquad \mathrm d'[u]=0
\]
is locally constant.
\end{proposition}

% Source: manuscript/editorial/solver_dossiers_20260919/
% p062_mixed_exact_tower_transfer_20260919/STATEMENT.tex.
\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:p062-mixed-exact-bundle-tower-transfer}
Let $K$ be a complete non-Archimedean field with nontrivial absolute
value, let $B_0$ be a positive-dimensional good, topologically separated,
pure strict $K$-analytic space, and let $\ell\geq1$.  Suppose that
\[
 B_\ell\xrightarrow{\pi_\ell}B_{\ell-1}
 \longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow B_1
 \xrightarrow{\pi_1}B_0
\]
is a finite tower in which every $B_j$ is a positive-dimensional good,
topologically separated, pure strict $K$-analytic space.  At every stage
assume that exactly one of the following descriptions is specified.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The morphism $\pi_j$ is a locally trivial standard strict
open-polydisc bundle as in
\Cref{prop:p062-open-polydisc-bundle-descent}; in particular, its positive
fibre dimension and chart radii satisfy the conditions there.
\item The base $B_{j-1}$ is locally holomorphically separated and
paracompact, and $\pi_j$ is a locally trivial analytic projective-space
bundle as in \Cref{prop:p062-projective-bundle-descent}, with fibre
$(\mathbf P_K^{q_j})^{\mathrm{an}}$ for some $q_j\geq1$.
\item The base $B_{j-1}$ is locally holomorphically separated and
paracompact, and $\pi_j$ is a locally trivial smooth proper split-toric
bundle as in
\Cref{prop:p062-smooth-proper-split-toric-bundle-descent}, with fibre
$X_{\Sigma_j}^{\mathrm{an}}$ for a smooth proper split toric $K$-variety
$X_{\Sigma_j}$ of dimension $q_j\geq1$.
\item The field $K$ is algebraically closed, the base $B_{j-1}$ is locally
holomorphically separated and paracompact, and $\pi_j$ is a locally trivial
proper smooth curve bundle as in
\Cref{prop:p062-proper-smooth-curve-bundle-descent}, with fibre
$D_j^{\mathrm{an}}$ for a nonempty geometrically connected smooth proper
algebraic $K$-curve $D_j$.
\end{enumerate}
Put $\Pi=\pi_1\circ\cdots\circ\pi_\ell$.  If
$h\in C^0(B_\ell,\mathbf R)$ satisfies
$\mathrm d'\mathrm d''[h]=0$, then there is a unique
$b\in C^0(B_0,\mathbf R)$ such that
\[
                  h=\Pi^*b,
                  \qquad \mathrm d'\mathrm d''[b]=0.
\]
The following properties transfer from $B_0$ to $B_\ell$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If every continuous zero-current function on $B_0$ is classically
pluriharmonic, then every such function on $B_\ell$ is classically
pluriharmonic.
\item If every continuous zero-current function on $B_0$ is
$\mathbf R$-harmonic, then every such function on $B_\ell$ is
$\mathbf R$-harmonic, hence locally $\mathbf R$-PL and
Gubler--Jell--Rabinoff harmonic.
\item If every $u\in C^0(B_0,\mathbf R)$ satisfying
\[
             \mathrm d'\mathrm d''[u]=0,
             \qquad \mathrm d'[u]=0
\]
is locally constant, then the same implication holds with $B_\ell$ in
place of $B_0$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

% Book-local P21.3 stage-local annular rigidity package, 20 September 2026.
\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:p062-stage-local-polyannulus-smooth-rigidity-transfer}
Let $K$ be a complete non-Archimedean field with nontrivial absolute value,
let $m\geq1$, and let $B$ be a good, topologically separated,
boundaryless, pure $m$-dimensional strict $K$-analytic space.  Let
$\pi:Y\to B$ be a morphism, where $Y$ is a good, topologically separated,
boundaryless, pure strict $K$-analytic space.  Suppose that $B$ has an
analytic open cover $\mathcal U$ such that, for every $U\in\mathcal U$,
the following conditions hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item There are an integer $s_U\geq1$, radii
\[
 0<r_{U,i}<R_{U,i},\qquad r_{U,i},R_{U,i}\in|K^\times|
 \quad(1\leq i\leq s_U),
\]
and an isomorphism over $U$
\[
 \pi^{-1}(U)\simeq
 U\times_K\prod_{i=1}^{s_U}
 \{z\in(\mathbf G_{\mathrm m,K})^{\mathrm{an}}:
                  r_{U,i}<|T_{U,i}(z)|<R_{U,i}\}.
\]
\item Every $b\in C^0(U,\mathbf R)$ satisfying
$\mathrm d'\mathrm d''[b]=0$ is classically pluriharmonic and ordinary
CLD-smooth, with $\mathrm d'\mathrm d''b=0$ as a smooth form.
\item Every $b\in C^0(U,\mathbf R)$ satisfying
\[
             \mathrm d'\mathrm d''[b]=0,
             \qquad \mathrm d'[b]=0
\]
is locally constant.
\end{enumerate}
Then every $h\in C^0(Y,\mathbf R)$ satisfying
$\mathrm d'\mathrm d''[h]=0$ is classically pluriharmonic and ordinary
CLD-smooth, with $\mathrm d'\mathrm d''h=0$ as a smooth form.  Moreover,
every such $h$ with $\mathrm d'[h]=0$ is locally constant.  No compatibility
among the displayed annular coordinates and no global logarithmic
coefficient formula are asserted.
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}
\label{thm:p213-residual-picard-stage-local-annular-tower}
Let $K,C,W$ be as in
\Cref{prop:p213-residual-picard-smooth-curve}, and assume
\eqref{eq:p213-residual-picard-vanishing}.  Let $\ell\geq1$, and suppose
that
\[
 B_\ell\xrightarrow{\pi_\ell}B_{\ell-1}
 \longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow B_1
 \xrightarrow{\pi_1}B_0=W
\]
is a finite tower in which every $B_j$ is a positive-dimensional good,
topologically separated, boundaryless, pure strict $K$-analytic space.
At every stage assume that exactly one of the following descriptions is
specified.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The morphism $\pi_j$ is one of the four exact bundle types appearing
in \Cref{prop:p062-mixed-exact-bundle-tower-transfer}, with all hypotheses
of the corresponding source proposition retained.
\item The morphism $\pi_j$ is an analytically locally trivial finite
standard strict open-polyannulus bundle, and there is a trivializing
analytic open cover $\mathcal U_j$ of $B_{j-1}$ such that every
$U\in\mathcal U_j$ satisfies conditions \textup{(2)} and \textup{(3)} of
\Cref{prop:p062-stage-local-polyannulus-smooth-rigidity-transfer}.
\end{enumerate}
Then every $h\in C^0(B_\ell,\mathbf R)$ satisfying
$\mathrm d'\mathrm d''[h]=0$ is classically pluriharmonic and ordinary
CLD-smooth, with $\mathrm d'\mathrm d''h=0$ as a smooth form.  Moreover,
every such $h$ with $\mathrm d'[h]=0$ is locally constant.

The stage-local hypotheses on the members of $\mathcal U_j$ are not
claimed to follow merely from the corresponding whole-space conclusions
on $B_{j-1}$.  In particular, the theorem does not assert the result for
an arbitrary locally trivial annular stage over an arbitrary intermediate
base open.
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}
\label{cor:p213-residual-picard-stage-local-annular-tower-bt}
In the setting of
\Cref{thm:p213-residual-picard-stage-local-annular-tower}, assume that
$B=B_\ell$ has pure dimension $n\geq2$.  Let $T$ be a positive
$\mathrm d'$- and $\mathrm d''$-closed ordinary CLD current of bidegree
$(p,p)$, $0\leq p\leq n-1$, and let $u,v\in C^0(B,\mathbf R)$ satisfy
\[
                         \mathrm d'\mathrm d''[u]
                         =\mathrm d'\mathrm d''[v].
\]
Then
\[
                         \mathrm d'\mathrm d''(uT)
                         =\mathrm d'\mathrm d''(vT).
\]
In particular, this holds for every continuous psh pair in the
continuous-potential predicate of P21.3.
\end{corollary}

\begin{corollary}
\label{cor:p213-residual-picard-stage-local-annular-tower-cover-bt}
Let $K$ be algebraically closed, complete, and nontrivially valued, let
$X$ be a good, topologically separated, pure, boundaryless strict
$K$-analytic space of dimension $n\geq2$, and let $V\subseteq X$ be
ordinary open.  Suppose that $V$ has an ordinary open cover by sets $B$
which, with their induced analytic structures, satisfy the geometric
hypotheses of
\Cref{cor:p213-residual-picard-stage-local-annular-tower-bt}.  Then every
positive closed ordinary CLD current $T$ of bidegree $(p,p)$ on $V$,
$0\leq p\leq n-1$, has Bedford--Taylor independence for every continuous
psh pair $u,v$ on $V$ with equal Hessian currents.
\end{corollary}

\begin{corollary}
\label{cor:p213-residual-picard-stage-local-annular-tower-basis-bt}
Let $K$ and $X$ be as in
\Cref{cor:p213-residual-picard-stage-local-annular-tower-cover-bt}.
Suppose that the ordinary topology of $X$ has a basis of open sets $B$ such
that every $B$, with its induced analytic structure, satisfies the
geometric hypotheses of
\Cref{cor:p213-residual-picard-stage-local-annular-tower-bt}.  Then the
continuous-pair Bedford--Taylor predicate in P21.3 holds on every ordinary
open subset of $X$ for every positive closed ordinary CLD current.
\end{corollary}
proof:
\begin{proof}[of
\Cref{prop:p062-stage-local-polyannulus-smooth-rigidity-transfer}]
Fix $U\in\mathcal U$ and use its displayed product chart.  The induced
analytic structure on $U$ is good, topologically separated, boundaryless,
pure, and strict.  Conditions \textup{(2)} and \textup{(3)} therefore imply
the two base hypotheses of
\Cref{prop:p062-open-polyannulus-rigid-base}.  Applied to
$h|_{\pi^{-1}(U)}$, that proposition gives unique continuous functions
$b_U,a_{U,1},\ldots,a_{U,s_U}$ on $U$ such that
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p062-stage-local-annular-formula}
 h|_{\pi^{-1}(U)}
 =\pi^*b_U+
   \sum_{i=1}^{s_U}(a_{U,i}\circ\pi)\log|T_{U,i}|,
 \qquad \mathrm d'\mathrm d''[b_U]=0,
\end{equation}
and every $a_{U,i}$ is locally constant.  The same proposition already
makes the restricted function classically pluriharmonic.

By condition \textup{(2)}, $b_U$ is ordinary CLD-smooth with zero smooth
Hessian.  Hence so is $\pi^*b_U$ by
\Cref{prop:cld-form-pullback}.  Every annular coordinate $T_{U,i}$ is
invertible, so
\Cref{lem:ch15-log-smooth,prop:cld-form-pullback} shows that its logarithm
in \eqref{eq:p062-stage-local-annular-formula} is ordinary CLD-smooth with
zero smooth Hessian.  Multiplication by the locally constant coefficient
$a_{U,i}\circ\pi$ preserves both properties.  Thus $h$ is ordinary
CLD-smooth with zero smooth Hessian on every $\pi^{-1}(U)$, and hence on
$Y$.

If also $\mathrm d'[h]=0$, the final assertion of
\Cref{prop:p062-open-polyannulus-rigid-base} makes
$h|_{\pi^{-1}(U)}$ locally constant for every $U$.  This is a local
property, so $h$ is locally constant on $Y$.  The proof used only the
individual product charts, which proves the final scope assertion.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[of
\Cref{thm:p213-residual-picard-stage-local-annular-tower}]
We prove by induction on $j$ the following three assertions on $B_j$:
every continuous zero-current function is classically pluriharmonic; every
such function is ordinary CLD-smooth with zero smooth Hessian; and adding
vanishing of its first current forces it to be locally constant.

For $j=0$, the first assertion is
\Cref{cor:ch19-continuous-zero-current-harmonic}, the second is
\Cref{prop:p213-residual-picard-smooth-curve}, and the third is
\Cref{lem:p062-curve-first-current-rigidity}.

Suppose the three assertions hold on $B_{j-1}$.  If $\pi_j$ is an exact
bundle stage, apply
\Cref{prop:p062-mixed-exact-bundle-tower-transfer} with a tower of length
one.  A zero-current function $h$ on $B_j$ has the form
\[
                              h=\pi_j^*b
\]
for a unique zero-current function $b$ on $B_{j-1}$.  The first transfer
assertion of that proposition and the induction hypothesis make $h$
classically pluriharmonic.  The induction smoothness assertion and
\Cref{prop:cld-form-pullback} make $h$ ordinary CLD-smooth with zero smooth
Hessian.  The third transfer assertion gives first-current rigidity on
$B_j$.

If $\pi_j$ is an annular stage, its specified cover and the induction
ambient hypotheses place it exactly in
\Cref{prop:p062-stage-local-polyannulus-smooth-rigidity-transfer}.  That
proposition supplies all three assertions on $B_j$.  This completes the
induction and proves the conclusions at $j=\ell$.

Notice that the induction supplies whole-space conclusions on each $B_j$;
it does not promote them to all ordinary opens of $B_j$.  The separately
stated conditions on every member of $\mathcal U_j$ are therefore used
essentially, proving the final qualification.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[of
\Cref{cor:p213-residual-picard-stage-local-annular-tower-bt}]
Put $h=u-v$.  Equality of the Hessian currents gives
$\mathrm d'\mathrm d''[h]=0$.  The tower theorem makes $h$ ordinary
CLD-smooth with zero smooth Hessian.  Apply \Cref{cor:ch16-smooth-h}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[of
\Cref{cor:p213-residual-picard-stage-local-annular-tower-cover-bt}]
Put $h=u-v$.  On every member $B$ of the displayed cover, apply
\Cref{thm:p213-residual-picard-stage-local-annular-tower} to $h|_B$.
Thus $h$ is ordinary CLD-smooth with zero smooth Hessian locally on $V$.
These are sheaf-local properties, so they hold on $V$.  Apply
\Cref{cor:ch16-smooth-h} directly to $T,u,v$ on $V$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[of
\Cref{cor:p213-residual-picard-stage-local-annular-tower-basis-bt}]
For an ordinary open $V\subseteq X$, the basis members contained in $V$
form a cover to which
\Cref{cor:p213-residual-picard-stage-local-annular-tower-cover-bt}
applies.
\end{proof}
